"'''Body Like a Back Road'''" is a song co-written and recorded by American [[country music]] singer [[Sam Hunt]]. It was released to country radio, by [[Music Corporation of America#MCA Nashville|MCA Nashville]] on February 2, 2017, as the lead single from his second studio album ''[[Southside (Sam Hunt album)|Southside]]''. The song is written by Hunt, [[Zach Crowell]], [[Shane McAnally]] and [[Josh Osborne]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Dukes|first1=Billy|title=Sam Hunt's New Song 'Body Like a Back Road' Written After Engagement [Listen]|url=http://tasteofcountry.com/sam-hunts-body-like-a-back-road-new-single/|access-date=January 25, 2017|work=[[Taste of Country]]|publisher=[[Townsquare Media]]|date=January 25, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Casey|first1=Jim|title=Sam Hunt Announces New "Body Like a Back Road" Single [Listen], New "15 in a 30 Tour" & Talks "Spiritual" Engagement Details|url=http://www.nashcountrydaily.com/2017/01/25/sam-hunt-announces-new-body-like-a-backroad-single-new-15-in-a-30-tour-talks-spiritual-engagement-details-2/|access-date=January 25, 2017|work=[[Nash Country Weekly]]|publisher=[[American Media (publisher)|American Media, Inc.]]|date=January 25, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170519060826/http://www.nashcountrydaily.com/2017/01/25/sam-hunt-announces-new-body-like-a-backroad-single-new-15-in-a-30-tour-talks-spiritual-engagement-details-2/|archive-date=May 19, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> It was released to American [[Adult contemporary music#Hot adult contemporary|adult pop]] radio on April 3, 2017, becoming his second [[Crossover music|crossover]] single promoted to a [[Contemporary hit radio|pop]] format.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hot/Modern/AC Future Releases|url=https://www.allaccess.com/hot-modern-ac/future-releases|publisher=All Access Media Group|access-date=April 5, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170404024856/https://www.allaccess.com/hot-modern-ac/future-releases|archive-date=April 4, 2017}}</ref>

Despite receiving mixed reviews, "Body Like a Back Road" became Hunt's most successful song to date. It broke two records within a month of one another; in early June 2017, the song was the longest running number one since [[Leroy Van Dyke]]'s "[[Walk On By (Leroy Van Dyke song)|Walk On By]]" 55 years earlier. With 20 weeks at number one on the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Hot Country Songs]] chart – this made Hunt the solo country artist with the second longest run at the top of the 59-year old Hot Country Songs chart. ([[Hank Snow]]'s, "[[I'm Moving On (Hank Snow song)|I'm Moving On]]" spent 21 weeks).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://theboot.com/sam-hunt-body-like-a-back-road-hot-country-songs-chart-record/ |title=Sam Hunt's 'Body Like a Back Road' Breaks 55-Year Hot Country Songs Chart Record|author= Angela Stefano |date=June 29, 2017 |work=The Boot }}</ref> The song broke records again in late July 2017, becoming the only song in the history of the Hot Country Songs chart to stay at number one for more than 24 weeks, a record previously held since 2012 by [[Florida Georgia Line]]'s "[[Cruise (song)|Cruise]]".<ref>{{cite news |url= https://www.usnews.com/news/entertainment/articles/2017-07-31/sam-hunt-makes-chart-history-with-body-like-a-back-road |title=Sam Hunt Makes Chart History With 'Body Like a Back Road'|first=Kristin M. |last=Hall|work=[[U.S. News & World Report]]|date=July 31, 2017 }}</ref> The song spent a total of 34 weeks on top of the Hot Country Songs chart. Additionally, the song peaked at number six on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], becoming Hunt's highest-charting single, and his first top 10 single overall, on that chart. With this peak, the song became the highest-charting country song on the US ''Billboard'' Hot 100 since "Cruise" by Florida Georgia Line, which reached number four in 2013.

"Body Like a Back Road" is a song co-written and recorded by American country music singer Sam Hunt. It was released to country radio, by MCA Nashville on February 2, 2017, as the lead single from his second studio album Southside. The song is written by Hunt, Zach Crowell, Shane McAnally and Josh Osborne. It was released to American adult pop radio on April 3, 2017, becoming his second crossover single promoted to a pop format.

Despite receiving mixed reviews, "Body Like a Back Road" became Hunt's most successful song to date. It broke two records within a month of one another; in early June 2017, the song was the longest running number one since Leroy Van Dyke's "Walk On By" 55 years earlier. With 20 weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot Country Songs chart – this made Hunt the solo country artist with the second longest run at the top of the 59-year old Hot Country Songs chart. (Hank Snow's, "I'm Moving On" spent 21 weeks). The song broke records again in late July 2017, becoming the only song in the history of the Hot Country Songs chart to stay at number one for more than 24 weeks, a record previously held since 2012 by Florida Georgia Line's "Cruise". The song spent a total of 34 weeks on top of the Hot Country Songs chart. Additionally, the song peaked at number six on the US Billboard Hot 100, becoming Hunt's highest-charting single, and his first top 10 single overall, on that chart. With this peak, the song became the highest-charting country song on the US Billboard Hot 100 since "Cruise" by Florida Georgia Line, which reached number four in 2013.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext: The song was written by Hunt with his producer Zach Crowell, Josh Osborne and Shane McAnally. According to Hunt, the song was written after his engagement to Hannah Lee Fowler. Hunt described it as "a lighthearted song" as he wanted to release something lighter than the "heavy direction" that his new album was taking. Hunt said: "I connect music to the emotions that come from relationships, so most of the songs that I write are inspired by those circumstances, emotions, feelings, all that kind of stuff".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nashcountrydaily.com/2017/01/25/sam-hunt-announces-new-body-like-a-backroad-single-new-15-in-a-30-tour-talks-spiritual-engagement-details-2/ |title=Sam Hunt Announces New "Body Like a Back Road" Single [Listen], New "15 in a 30 Tour" & Talks "Spiritual" Engagement Details |first=Jim |last=Casey |work=Nash Country Daily |date=January 25, 2017 |access-date=February 10, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170519060826/http://www.nashcountrydaily.com/2017/01/25/sam-hunt-announces-new-body-like-a-backroad-single-new-15-in-a-30-tour-talks-spiritual-engagement-details-2/ |archive-date=May 19, 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He had previously broken up with Fowler, and wrote "Drinkin' Too Much" as an apology (the break-up also inspired a few other songs in ''[[Montevallo (album)|Montevallo]]'').<ref>{{cite news|last1=Stefano|first1=Angela|title=Sam Hunt Drops Brand-New Song, 'Drinkin' Too Much' [LISTEN]|url=http://theboot.com/sam-hunt-drinkin-too-much/|work=The Boot|publisher=[[Townsquare Media]]|date=January 1, 2017}}</ref> The couple got back together, and a few days after "Drinkin' Too Much" was released in January 2017, he announced their engagement.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/country/news/hear-sam-hunts-breezy-new-song-body-like-a-back-road-w464324 |title=Hear Sam Hunt's Breezy New Song 'Body Like a Back Road' | first=Brittney|last= McKenna|date=February 1, 2017|magazine=Rolling Stone }}</ref>
sections.text: The song was written by Hunt with his producer Zach Crowell, Josh Osborne and Shane McAnally. According to Hunt, the song was written after his engagement to Hannah Lee Fowler. Hunt described it as "a lighthearted song" as he wanted to release something lighter than the "heavy direction" that his new album was taking. Hunt said: "I connect music to the emotions that come from relationships, so most of the songs that I write are inspired by those circumstances, emotions, feelings, all that kind of stuff". He had previously broken up with Fowler, and wrote "Drinkin' Too Much" as an apology (the break-up also inspired a few other songs in Montevallo). The couple got back together, and a few days after "Drinkin' Too Much" was released in January 2017, he announced their engagement.

sections.heading: Composition
sections.wikitext: The song is composed in the key of [[F major]] with a tempo of 96–100 beats per minute.<ref>[https://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/mtd.asp?ppn=MN0171408 "Body Like a Back Road" sheet music at musicnotes.com]</ref>

sections.heading: Commercial performance
sections.wikitext:
In the US, the song reached number one on the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Hot Country Songs]] chart and remained there for 34 consecutive weeks until it was knocked off by "[[What Ifs]]" performed by [[Kane Brown]] and [[Lauren Alaina]],<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/kane-brown-what-ifs-lauren-alaina-sam-hunt-hot-country-songs-chart/ |title= Kane Brown's 'What Ifs' Featuring Lauren Alaina Tops Hot Country Songs, Stopping Sam Hunt's Record Run |date=October 10, 2017 |first= Jim |last=Asker|magazine=Billboard}}</ref> breaking the record set by "[[Cruise (song)|Cruise]]" by [[Florida Georgia Line]] for the most weeks atop the chart (24 weeks).<ref name="25 weeks">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/sam-hunt-breaks-record-hot-country-songs-chart-body-like-a-back-road/|title=Sam Hunt's 'Body Like a Back Road' Breaks Record for Most Weeks Atop Hot Country Songs Chart|magazine=Billboard|last=Asker|first=Jim|date=August 1, 2017|access-date=August 2, 2017}}</ref> The record was later broken by [[Bebe Rexha]] and [[Florida Georgia Line]]'s collaboration "[[Meant to Be (Bebe Rexha song)|Meant to Be]]" which stayed atop the chart for 50 consecutive weeks. It is Hunt's longest chart-topping single, overtaking "[[Take Your Time (Sam Hunt song)|Take Your Time]]", which stayed on top of the Hot Country Songs chart for 11 weeks.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/brad-paisley-sam-hunt-john-mayer-country-charts/ |title=Brad Paisley's 'War' Breaks Out at No. 1; John Mayer Makes Country Chart Debut |date=May 2, 2017 |first= Jim |last=Asker|magazine=Billboard }}</ref>

"Body Like a Back Road" also reached number one on the [[Country Airplay]] chart and stayed at that spot for three consecutive weeks. On the week after Hunt's performance at the [[Academy of Country Music Awards|ACM Awards]], the song sold 70,000 copies and jumped up six places from number 12 to number six on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], becoming Hunt's highest-charting single, and his first top 10 single overall, on that chart. With this peak, the song became the highest-charting country song on the US ''Billboard'' Hot 100 since "[[Cruise (song)|Cruise]]" by [[Florida Georgia Line]], which reached number four in 2013.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/hot-100-ed-sheeran-shape-of-you-kendrick-lamar-humble-debut-sam-hunt/|title=Ed Sheeran Stays No. 1 on Hot 100, Kendrick Lamar Debuts at No. 2|magazine=Billboard|last=Trust|first=Gary|date=April 10, 2017|access-date=April 11, 2017}}</ref> The song also crossed over to pop radio.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/sam-hunt-body-like-a-back-road-country-song-pop-radio/ |title=Sam Hunt's Country Hit 'Body Like a Back Road' Speeds to Pop Radio|date=April 7, 2017 |first= Gary |last=Trust }}</ref>

The song was certified Diamond on July 28, 2023.<ref name="RIAA"/> It was the third best-selling song in the US in 2017, and the best-selling country song, with 1,818,000 copies (3,723,000 units including streams) sold in the year.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/money/2018/01/04/country-musics-most-listened-artists-chris-stapleton-luke-bryan-thomas-rhett-2017/1003648001/ |title=Revealed: Country music's most listened to artists in 2017 |first=Nate|last= Rau |work=[[The Tennessean]] |date= January 4, 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/ed-sheeran-divide-nielsen-music-top-album-2017/|title=Ed Sheeran's 'Divide' Is Nielsen Music's Top Album of 2017 in U.S.|author=Keith Caulfield|magazine=Billboard|date=3 January 2018|access-date=January 4, 2018}}</ref> It has sold 1,951,000 copies in the United States as of June 2018.<ref name="us sales">{{cite news|url=http://roughstock.com/news/2018/06/43084-top-30-digital-country-singles-june-6-2018|title=Top 30 Digital Country Singles: June 6, 2018 |work=Roughstock|last=Bjorke|first=Matt|date=June 5, 2018 |access-date=June 7, 2018 }}</ref>
sections.text:
In the US, the song reached number one on the Billboard Hot Country Songs chart and remained there for 34 consecutive weeks until it was knocked off by "What Ifs" performed by Kane Brown and Lauren Alaina, breaking the record set by "Cruise" by Florida Georgia Line for the most weeks atop the chart (24 weeks). The record was later broken by Bebe Rexha and Florida Georgia Line's collaboration "Meant to Be" which stayed atop the chart for 50 consecutive weeks. It is Hunt's longest chart-topping single, overtaking "Take Your Time", which stayed on top of the Hot Country Songs chart for 11 weeks.

"Body Like a Back Road" also reached number one on the Country Airplay chart and stayed at that spot for three consecutive weeks. On the week after Hunt's performance at the ACM Awards, the song sold 70,000 copies and jumped up six places from number 12 to number six on the US Billboard Hot 100, becoming Hunt's highest-charting single, and his first top 10 single overall, on that chart. With this peak, the song became the highest-charting country song on the US Billboard Hot 100 since "Cruise" by Florida Georgia Line, which reached number four in 2013. The song also crossed over to pop radio.

The song was certified Diamond on July 28, 2023. It was the third best-selling song in the US in 2017, and the best-selling country song, with 1,818,000 copies (3,723,000 units including streams) sold in the year. It has sold 1,951,000 copies in the United States as of June 2018.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: Despite huge commercial success, "Body Like a Back Road" was met with overwhelmingly mixed-to-negative reviews. It has been in the midst of controversy and being called out by some reporters and [[Neotraditional country|neo-traditional country]] artists for lack of similarity to country music's "roots".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/entry/sam-hunt-body-like-a-back-road-grammy-nomination_us_5a1f2c7ee4b0a8581e67ad0b|title=The Most Upsetting Grammy Nominee Is Sam Hunt's 'Body Like A Back Road'|first=Travis|last=Waldron|date=November 30, 2017|access-date=December 18, 2017|work=[[HuffPost]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theringer.com/2017/08/25/pop-culture/sam-hunt-future-of-country-music|title=Sam Hunt Is the Future of Country Music |website=[[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]]|access-date=December 18, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/country/news/aaron-lewis-says-luke-bryan-sam-hunt-are-choking-country-w439683|title=Aaron Lewis Says Luke Bryan, Sam Hunt Are 'Choking' Country Music|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|date=14 September 2016 |access-date=December 18, 2017}}</ref> Many also took issue with the comparison between a woman's body and a back road. Multiple critics have cited "Body Like a Back Road" as one of the worst songs of 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.craveonline.com/mandatory/1354557-ranking-11-worst-songs-2017#/slide/2|title=Ranking The 11 Worst Songs Of 2017|date=19 December 2017|access-date=21 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171222063411/http://www.craveonline.com/mandatory/1354557-ranking-11-worst-songs-2017#/slide/2|archive-date=22 December 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://beat.media/7-worst-songs-of-2017|title=7 Worst Songs of 2017|first=Matt|last=Knight|website=beat.media|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171222052305/https://beat.media/7-worst-songs-of-2017|archive-date=22 December 2017|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://time.com/5048308/top-10-worst-songs-2017/|title=The Top 10 Worst Songs of 2017|date=December 22, 2017|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|access-date=December 23, 2017}}</ref>
sections.text: Despite huge commercial success, "Body Like a Back Road" was met with overwhelmingly mixed-to-negative reviews. It has been in the midst of controversy and being called out by some reporters and neo-traditional country artists for lack of similarity to country music's "roots". Many also took issue with the comparison between a woman's body and a back road. Multiple critics have cited "Body Like a Back Road" as one of the worst songs of 2017.
